summary: Iter6 tested the 12 pre-deployment improvements (admin username+password auth, forgot/reset, multi-admin CRUD, audit log, analytics dashboard, transactional emailer guardrails, and 3 new public routes: /terms, /privacy, /account/recover). 31/31 new backend pytest cases pass, plus a full regression of Iter5's 12 tests (43/43 total). Playwright verified: admin login bad-pw shows inline error, correct login redirects to /admin/licenses, /admin dashboard loads without crash, all 3 new public pages render with correct <title>/<h1>, /admin/forgot request form returns the generic 'if the account exists' message without user enumeration, and useSEO hook sets per-page titles cleanly. Also verified robots.txt now includes /admin* and /r/ disallows plus the sitemap directive.

minor.issue: Only returns is_admin=true for the root ADMIN_USERNAME — a valid non-root admin_users owner/reviewer gets is_admin=false. /api/admin/session correctly returns authenticated=true for both; the Navbar guard should probably use /admin/session (or /admin/me should mirror it). Not blocking since only root admin exists today, but will break multi-admin UX once a second admin is added.

Rewrites backend/.env in place using Path.read_text/write_text — no lock/tmpfile+rename, so a concurrent .env writer would race. Low risk in prod (single-writer), but the /app/scripts/ startup should avoid touching that key. Also note: the file loses any trailing blank lines and re-normalises to LF endings.
Uses asyncio.get_event_loop().create_task inside a running FastAPI request; on newer asyncio this emits DeprecationWarning. Prefer `asyncio.create_task(...)` directly (already inside an event loop).

action_items: Fix /api/admin/me to trust the admin_users table (mirror /api/admin/session) so non-root admins also see is_admin=true.
Replace `asyncio.get_event_loop().create_task` in /admin/forgot with `asyncio.create_task` to silence DeprecationWarning.
Consider atomic .env rewrite (tmpfile + os.replace) in /admin/reset-password to protect against partial writes.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 2858 lines — monolithic. Split into auth, admin, jobs, payments, referrals, map, blog modules. Every new iteration compounds risk.
backend/emailer.py `_fire_and_forget` calls asyncio.run() as fallback which would deadlock if reached from a sync path inside an already-running loop; guard with try/except and log-and-drop instead.
Recovery reset tokens are stored plaintext in db.admin_reset_tokens — even though they're one-time and 30-min, prefer hashing (sha256) at rest so a DB dump doesn't leak live reset tokens.
/api/admin/audit has no pagination cursor — the limit param caps at 500 but there is no offset/since filter for older records; fine for MVP.
Rate limiter is in-process and per-IP only; if backend restarts or scales horizontally, brute-force protection resets. Not a blocker for single-instance k8s deployment but worth noting for prod.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (9/9 flows: admin bad login, admin good login, /admin, /terms, /privacy, /account/recover, recover-google-btn, admin-forgot request form, forgot generic response)
